findings: BRIDGES 5/18 sentences (28%) connect to the one before. The approved iPhone 18 Pro script runs 53%; the weak generation of the same story ran 9%. A sentence that starts a new subject with no bridge reads as the next bullet, not the next beat. (framework S9, S22)
WHAT WITHOUT SO WHAT 1/1 spec sentences never say what the number does for the viewer. "2nm chip" is information; "faster without draining the battery" is relevance. (framework S7)
CADENCE: only 1 sentence reaches 18 words (longest 20). The playbook asks for 'occasionally one long spec sentence' — with everything short, nothing reads as short. Nothing to push against.
NUMBERS: one every 6.3 sentences. The playbook asks for one every 2-3 — concrete numbers are what make a claim feel reported rather than asserted.
HUMANIZER: recorded for this draft. The checks above are the measurable half; the `humanizer` pass is the half that decides whether it sounds like a person.
research_advice: the most surprising claim (SURPRISE 85: 'Guests open the link in a computer browser. Mobile browsers ') is spoken in the last 40% of the script — consider leading with it.
